hypotheses.claim: The already-researched generic function-definition contract can be integrated into the D parser candidate and canonical typed IR without new FRANK-specific semantics.
hypotheses.prediction: Full D legacy corpus plus typed fn programs parse; exact call binding/type checks fail closed; canonical meaning remains stable under formatting; lowering agrees with reference evaluator.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Existing rule/needle/cycle/host constructs already provide equivalent general reusable definition->call semantics, so fn surface is unnecessary.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production admitted compiler demonstrates equivalent deterministic typed definition/call closure without fn, or fn integration causes unavoidable semantic ambiguity/regression.

hypotheses.claim: Exact symbol/signature resolution should be a canonical IR/compiler relation, never associative graph/DB/GWT/model fallback.
hypotheses.prediction: Missing or incompatible calls reject deterministically; fuzzy fallback cannot improve correctness without violating identity guarantees.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Associative resolution can safely recover unresolved call targets.
hypotheses.falsifier: A preregistered compiler corpus shows associative recovery is deterministic, provenance-preserving, ambiguity-safe and outperforms exact resolution without false binding.

hypotheses.claim: semantic_hash and provenance-bound contract_hash must remain distinct through source normalization and lowering.
hypotheses.prediction: Formatting/comment variants retain semantic_hash while exact source/contract hash changes; semantic mutations alter semantic_hash.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One hash is sufficient for both meaning and exact source contract identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Replay/source-chain requirements can be met without ambiguity or provenance loss using one identity across formatting and semantic mutation cases.

hypotheses.claim: Strict-LALR conflict debt is an independent parser-hardening problem and should not be hidden by successful non-strict execution.
hypotheses.prediction: The baseline D candidate and D+fn both fail strict conflict checking under the current Lark toolchain while deterministic non-strict execution still passes bounded tests.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Strict-mode conflicts are irrelevant implementation noise and never affect production diagnostics or parse stability.
hypotheses.falsifier: A conflict-free admitted grammar/parser is produced and exhaustive/ambiguity/fuzz tests show the prior conflicts had no semantic or diagnostic consequences.
